At President Donald J. Trump’s direction, the Administration is pursuing a coordinated, whole-of-government effort to modernize federal systems, strengthen our defenses, and protect America’s critical infrastructure. The Trump Administration has assembled a highly capable interagency team that remains hypervigilant in protecting our nation’s critical systems, confronting emerging threats, and ensuring America is secure, resilient, and positioned to lead in the digital age.

As part of his historic effort to strengthen America’s cyber capabilities, President Trump has established new leadership structures, made key appointments, and expanded the cyber workforce. He has nominated battle-tested cyber leader and Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies to lead the Office of the National Cyber Director, which will be integrated into a reorganized White House operational and policy structure, and he appointed General Joshua M. Rudd to lead the National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management’s United States Tech Force has brought in nearly 500 high-skilled engineers to modernize and secure essential systems across the government. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added more than 200 personnel to mission-critical roles, and will have more than 400 additional personnel added in the coming months.

Recognizing the strategic importance of winning the Super Intelligence (SI) race, President Trump established the Super Intelligence Force, chaired by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. The Force is advancing American leadership in SI, maintaining our technological advantage over foreign adversaries, and helping safeguard our critical infrastructure. By leveraging SI and assembling top experts across each federal agency, the Administration is supercharging its ability to identify, deter, and disrupt malicious activity before it can ever compromise our systems.

President Trump is committed to ensuring our systems remain secure, resilient, and reliable and has taken a historic all-of-government approach to deliver on his cyber agenda:

  • BUILDING AN ELITE CYBERSECURITY TEAM AND ORGANIZATION: President Trump established the Super Intelligence Force, nominated highly-qualified Kirsten Davies to lead the Office of the National Cyber Director, and he selected General Joshua M. Rudd to helm the NSA and U.S. Cyber Command. The White House cyber policy and operations teams are rapidly staffing up with additional experts and will be reorganized under the National Security Council and Homeland Security Council to ensure effective integration across all government cybersecurity programs. CISA has waived otherwise applicable limits on its hiring to scale up employment, adding more than 200 mission-critical personnel, with another 400-plus expected. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management’s new United States Tech Force has hired nearly 500 highly-skilled, private sector engineers to modernize and secure government systems across every major agency in under a year.
  • PROTECTING THE SYSTEMS AMERICANS DEPEND ON: CISA launched CI Fortify to help critical infrastructure operators maintain essential services during major disruptions and established a requirement for federal agencies to aggressively patch high-risk vulnerabilities within three days. Next week, DOJ and FBI will unveil their latest cyber defense initiative as a follow on to Operation Winter SHIELD.
  • SECURING AMERICA’S NETWORKS: The FCC prohibited new foreign-made consumer routers identified as posing unacceptable national security risks, while federal agencies are also strengthening protections for telecommunications and transportation infrastructure.
  • CRACKING DOWN ON CYBERCRIME: Federal law enforcement has made more than 150 cybercrime arrests, disrupted more than 220 malicious cyber operations, and extradited more than 50 cyber actors in 2026 alone.
  • DISMANTLING GLOBAL SCAM OPERATIONS AND SAVING AMERICANS BILLIONS: Just yesterday, the Department of Justice announced that it has brought more than 400 cases against criminal scam networks since March 2026, identifying more than $8 billion in intended fraud losses. The FBI’s Operation Blackout has seized nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, taken control of more than 14,000 digital devices, and dismantled 29 scam compounds across four continents. Federal law enforcement has also helped prevent at least $1.6 billion in losses by warning more than 10,000 potential victims, frozen nearly $1 billion in cryptocurrency tied to foreign scammers, and worked with technology companies to disrupt millions of criminal online accounts. 
  • HELPING PROTECT AMERICA’S BUSINESSES IN THE DIGITAL AGE: The Trump Administration is implementing GOLD EAGLE to coordinate cybersecurity vulnerability identification across critical infrastructure sectors and expanding private-sector access to advanced models to strengthen defenses.
  • HOLDING FOREIGN HACKERS ACCOUNTABLE: The Department of Justice charged 12 Chinese hackers and law enforcement officers for their alleged roles in global hacking campaigns targeting U.S. agencies. Treasury also sanctioned four entities supporting ransomware attacks against Americans and five Iranian nationals for targeting U.S. critical infrastructure, government offices, and digital assets.
  • STRENGTHENING AMERICA’S MILITARY CYBER DEFENSES: President Trump modernized cybersecurity standards for America’s military and intelligence systems for the first time in more than 35 years.
  • LEADING THE WORLD IN SUPER INTELLIGENCE, STOPPING HACKERS AND FOREIGN THREATS: The Trump Administration is working with leading technology companies to test advanced models, identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and strengthen defenses before adversaries can exploit weaknesses.
  • PROTECTING AMERICA’S CHILDREN ONLINE: The Trump Administration is aggressively confronting the digital extortion rackets that have wrecked the lives of too many young people, a top priority for First Lady Melania Trump, who led a successful bipartisan effort to pass the Take It Down Act. 

Under President Trump’s leadership, America is strengthening its defenses, investing in its people and technology, and ensuring our critical infrastructure remains secure and resilient.
